text:
tara: hey all, first-week blocker. running our docker-compose on Fedora (rootless docker / dockerd with userns remap) and Postgres fails on init: "initdb: could not change permissions of directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data": Permission denied". i'm using a host bind ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data because i want DB files on disk. any tips?

matt: welcome! :wave: this is a classic user namespace remapping problem. with userns remap enabled, root inside the container maps to an unprivileged range on the host (e.g., 100000+). so UID 999 in the container becomes 100999 on the host.

tara: i tried `sudo chown 999:999 ./pgdata` but host still shows owner uid 100025 (weird numbers).

matt: that matches: your dockerd configuration probably maps to a different subuid range (check /etc/subuid for the dockerd user, often `dockremap:100000:65536`). host owner = mapping_start + container_uid. Example: mapping_start 100000 + postgres uid 999 -> 100999. So `sudo chown -R 100999:100999 ./pgdata` should align the host dir to the mapped uid.

sam: quick checks: `ls -ln ./pgdata` to see numeric owner, `docker info | grep -i userns` to confirm remap. Another safe workaround is to use a named volume in compose to avoid host FS at all:

```
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data

volumes:
  pgdata:
```

That sidesteps mapping headaches for dev.

tara: is there a helper command to find the correct host uid so i don't have to math it manually?

matt: yep. You can inspect /etc/subuid for the dockerd user or run a helper container that prints both IDs. Example: `docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/pgdata":/data postgres:15 sh -c "id -u postgres && ls -ln /data || true"`. The first number is the container uid, and ls -ln shows how it appears on host (it will show the remapped numeric owner). Then set host chown accordingly.

sam: one-shot chown from inside a container also works because the daemon will map it. For instance: `docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/pgdata":/data --entrypoint sh postgres:15 -c "chown -R 999:999 /data"`. That will create the right remapped owner on host if the daemon userns remap is active.

tara: tried the helper, found mapping_start 100000 and postgres uid 999 -> 100999. ran `sudo chown -R 100999:100999 ./pgdata` and `chmod 700 ./pgdata`. Postgres init started. thanks!!

matt: nice. for long term: either use named volumes for dev or add a README note for folks running rootless/userns docker. Also avoid forcing `platform:` or other opts that complicate parity.

infra-bot: onboarding reminder: if you're on distributions with rootless docker or dockerd userns remap, dev checklist recommends named volumes for DBs or documenting the UID mapping. See internal guide: https://intranet.redwood.dev/dev-setup#local-db

tara: switching to a named volume for day-to-day dev and keeping a small host dump file for backups. appreciate the quick help :tada:
